lines.text: Dave Ramsey makes retirement sound simple.
Earn 12%. Inflation takes 4%. Live off 8%.
lines.say: Earn twelve percent. Inflation takes four. Live off eight.

lines.text: $40,000 a year takes just $500,000.
lines.say: Forty thousand a year takes just five hundred thousand.

lines.text: Joe and Suzy save $625 a month, age 30 to 70.
lines.say: Joe and Suzy save six twenty-five a month, age thirty to seventy.

lines.text: The book says: $7.59 million.
lines.say: The book says: seven point five nine million dollars.

lines.text: What if I'm half wrong? Four million. Six times wrong?
Let's check, against real history.
First: do prices rise 4% a year?
lines.say: First: do prices rise four percent a year?

lines.text: Since 1926, about 2.9%. Since the book, 2.6%.
lines.say: Since nineteen twenty-six, about two point nine. Since the book, two point six.

lines.text: That one holds up.
Next, the 12%. Up 30, down 10, up 25, up 3. That averages 12%.
lines.say: Next, the twelve percent. Up thirty, down ten, up twenty-five, up three. That averages twelve.

lines.text: But $10,000 grows as if it earned 10.8%.
lines.say: But ten thousand dollars grows as if it earned ten point eight.

lines.text: From 1926 to 2002, the S&P 500 averaged 11.9%, but compounded 10%.
lines.say: From nineteen twenty-six to two thousand two, the S and P averaged eleven point nine, but compounded ten.

lines.text: Since 1981, no 30-year stretch compounded 12%. Half right.
lines.say: Since nineteen eighty-one, no thirty-year stretch compounded twelve. Half right.

lines.text: Now Joe and Suzy, through all six real 40-year stretches since 1981.
lines.say: Now Joe and Suzy, through all six real forty-year stretches since nineteen eighty-one.

lines.text: $625 a month became $3.6 to $5.9 million. Never $7.6. Half wrong.
lines.say: Six twenty-five a month became three point six to five point nine million. Never seven point six. Half wrong.

lines.text: After inflation: $1.2 to $2 million. Closer to six times wrong.
lines.say: After inflation: one point two to two million. Closer to six times wrong.

lines.text: Even a steady 12% makes only $6.1 million.
lines.say: Even a steady twelve percent makes only six point one million.

lines.text: Then the 8%. Picture a perfect world: 12% and 4%, every year.
lines.say: Then the eight percent. Picture a perfect world: twelve and four, every year.

lines.text: $40,000 from $500,000, paid monthly, runs out in year 38.
lines.say: Forty thousand from five hundred thousand, paid monthly, runs out in year thirty-eight.

lines.text: The most that lasts is 7.52%. $40,000 needs about $532,000.
lines.say: The most that lasts is seven point five two percent. Forty thousand needs about five hundred thirty-two thousand.

lines.text: Now real markets, with real inflation.
Since 1981, 11 of 16 thirty-year S&P retirements kept up.
lines.say: Since nineteen eighty-one, eleven of sixteen thirty-year S and P retirements kept up.

lines.text: Back to 1926, just 29 of 71. 35 ran out.
lines.say: Back to nineteen twenty-six, just twenty-nine of seventy-one. Thirty-five ran out.

lines.text: Everyone who retired from 2004 to 2008 ran out or fell behind.
lines.say: Everyone who retired from two thousand four to two thousand eight ran out, or fell behind.

lines.text: The year you start matters most.
So, half wrong? About that, yes.
Saving still beats not saving, by a mile.
The numbers are just too tidy.
